clue.text: On soldiers getting the needle, shows of force appear

parts.note: anything on the subject of soldiers or the army is military in nature
body art inked by a needle: these are what the skin gets from it

explanation.surface: Soldiers queue at the parlour for ink, which is how armed forces display themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting the needle' suggests irritation, but here it is literal needlework on skin. A military tattoo is also an evening display of marching bands and drill, like the Edinburgh one.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening displays of drumming, marching and drill by troops are spectacles showing off a nation's armed strength.

clue.text: Had a bad employer so treated

definitions.text: Had a bad employer so treated

parts.words: Had a bad employer so treated
parts.note: a worker exploited by an unfair boss has been handled wrongly or exploited

explanation.surface: A worker grumbles about how a poor boss handled them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exploited by a bad boss means being treated wrongly, put to improper use.

clue.text: Vessel-an unarmed cruiser

definitions.meaning: a large passenger ship is a vessel
an ocean-going passenger ship cruises but carries no guns, unlike a naval cruiser

explanation.surface: A ship is described as a warship type without weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A big passenger ship is a vessel, and it cruises the seas without any armament.

clue.text: In advance, gave warning brought down from on high!

definitions.meaning: to alert someone beforehand with a quiet word
knocked over and toppled from a raised position

explanation.surface: Someone warned ahead of time, or something was knocked off a height.
explanation.definitionFit: To alert someone secretly is idiom for a warning; literally, tilting something off its perch topples it.

clue.text: Reunite broken up group of followers

indicators.note: a thing broken up has its parts scattered, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band that split reunites its entourage of fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken up' tells you to rearrange the letters of REUNITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the band of attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: Bound to have faith in something, we hear

indicators.note: something we hear is spoken, so the sound of the phrase before is what counts

parts.note: to have relied on something with confidence is to have trusted it

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to believe in a thing, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but Bound is the definition: tied up. 'we hear' gives the sound of TRUSTED, spelt TRUSSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up tightly with rope, like a chicken readied for the oven.

clue.text: Subject for discussion: damaged nerve that's sighted

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nerve carrying vision from eye to brain is the optic nerve, so a sighted nerve is optic

explanation.surface: A meeting discusses an injury to the nerve that gives sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges OPTIC, the word for the nerve of sight, so the anagram is of a word you must first supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme or matter that people talk about is their discussion's subject.

clue.text: Man thus starts emergency procedures at sea!

definitions.text: Man thus starts emergency procedures at sea!

parts.words: Man thus starts emergency procedures at sea!
parts.note: the shout raised when a sailor falls into the water begins with 'Man', and the missing word says where he went

explanation.surface: A crew springs into action at a cry from the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry 'Man ...!' at sea sets off a rescue; the answer is the word that completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The alarm shout completing 'Man ...' means someone has fallen off the ship into the water.

clue.text: Sole supporters with bands going on foot

definitions.text: Sole supporters with bands going on foot

parts.words: Sole supporters with bands going on foot
parts.note: light shoes with a sole held on by straps over the foot

explanation.surface: Fans of a lone cause march along with marching bands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole supporters' reads like the only fans of something; it means things that support the soles of the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Open summer shoes are soles held on by straps over the foot.

clue.text: And about old roasting equipment used for child's play

indicators.note: one piece goes about another, wrapping round it

parts.note: a rotating rod for roasting meat over a fire, an old-fashioned cooking tool

explanation.surface: Antique roasting gear is found among toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' belongs with the roasting gear, since spits are old-fashioned, not a signal for O or EX; the definition describes where children play.
explanation.definitionFit: A box of sand in a playground or garden where small children dig and play.

clue.text: It doesn't describe a number-that's definite

definitions.text: It doesn't describe a number-that's definite

parts.words: It doesn't describe a number-that's definite
parts.note: a word for a large but unspecified count, so the number it gives is never exact

explanation.surface: Someone insists, firmly, that a word is not about numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's definite' reads as an emphatic aside, but it belongs with 'a number': the word never gives a definite number.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial for very many, an indeterminate large quantity.

clue.text: They're armed with bars to keep order in camp

definitions.text: They're armed with bars to keep order in camp

parts.words: They're armed with bars to keep order in camp
parts.note: non-commissioned officers wear stripes on the arm and maintain discipline in barracks

explanation.surface: Guards with metal rods keep the peace in a prison camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'armed with bars' suggests weapons; it means wearing stripes (chevrons) on the arm, as these NCOs do.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-commissioned army officers wear three chevrons on the sleeve and enforce discipline.

clue.text: Horse gunners killing people in India, for instance

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

explanation.surface: Mounted artillerymen are slaughtering locals in colonial India.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the creature by example: a venomous snake that kills many people in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous hooded snake that causes many deaths by its bite on the subcontinent.

clue.text: Brodie's about to take off his clothes

indicators.note: about can mean round and about, so the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, all seven letters used

explanation.surface: Brodie is on the verge of stripping off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'about to', but it is the anagram signal working on BRODIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To undress, removing one's robes or garments.

clue.text: Little but lethal-certainly not big shot

definitions.text: Little but lethal-certainly not big shot

parts.words: Little but lethal-certainly not big shot
parts.note: hand-held firearms are small yet deadly, and fire nothing like artillery shells

explanation.surface: A small but dangerous person is definitely no bigwig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big shot' reads as an important person; here it means heavy artillery ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and rifles are compact personal weapons, deadly though not heavy guns.

clue.text: Sustained attacks by the enemy being successful!

definitions.text: Sustained attacks by the enemy being successful!

parts.words: Sustained attacks by the enemy being successful!
parts.note: when an enemy's onslaught succeeds, it beats the side it attacks

explanation.surface: Long enemy offensives are paying off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sustained' reads as 'prolonged', but also as 'suffered': one who has sustained successful attacks has been beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Losses suffered in battle, when the enemy beats you.

clue.text: Company has the last word and the first place for the stars

parts.note: a firm is a business company
the word said at the end of a prayer

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: A business has its final say and pole position for celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the stars' suggests celebrities, but they are in the night sky. 'first' takes T from the second 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The vault of the heavens, the sky where stars appear.

clue.text: Frightened, if classy raffle goes wrong

indicators.note: a thing that goes wrong is muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Someone is scared that a posh prize draw will go awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' scrambles U and RAFFLE. U for upper-class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of fear, scared.

clue.text: Linked with footholds, could one say?

definitions.text: Linked with footholds, could one say?

parts.words: Linked with footholds, could one say?
parts.note: chains that hold the feet, so a playful word for them is footholds

explanation.surface: A climber asks whether these are attached to grips on the rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'footholds' suggests climbing; here it means things that hold feet, linked chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains or shackles fastened round a prisoner's ankles.

clue.text: Hung around, being glued on? Wrong!

indicators.note: set wrongly, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly thought a thing was stuck fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong!' rearranges GLUEDON.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf about idly, lazing around.

clue.text: May well march on these troops

definitions.text: May well march on these troops

parts.words: May well march on these troops
parts.note: soldiers march on drill grounds, and march in ceremonial processions

explanation.surface: Soldiers are likely to march on a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troops' looks like the subject; read 'troops may well march on these'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parade grounds and processions are where troops march.

clue.text: On the quiet, responsible for not being very rigid

parts.note: p is the musical mark piano, meaning softly
liable means legally responsible

explanation.surface: Secretly answerable for a lack of firmness.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quiet is the musical abbreviation piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily bent, flexible.

clue.text: Genuine Screen One production

indicators.note: a production makes something new from the material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An authentic production on the first television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges SCREEN with I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: Honest and true, without pretence.

clue.text: Works on land registers

explanation.surface: A farmer's labour and a shop's machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer cultivates soil; shop cash drawers are cash registers.

clue.text: Maybe happy to look like this

definitions.text: Maybe happy to look like this

parts.words: Maybe happy to look like this
parts.note: a cheerful expression is how a happy person looks

explanation.surface: Someone might be pleased with their appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleased facial expression with the mouth turned up.

clue.text: Aunt Ira in trouble, being religious

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Aunt Ira has run into difficulties because of her faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' looks like the indicator, but 'in' is part of the fodder: AUNTIRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a Christian denomination that rejects the Trinity.

clue.text: Mythical character to fix Ionian part

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A legendary figure repairs a piece of Greek coastline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' points to the letters within fIX IONian.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend, a king bound to a burning wheel in Hades.

clue.text: Making a mistake about a decorating circle

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it

parts.note: erring means making a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone blunders when it comes to ornamental hoops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ERRING around A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental loop worn in the lobe of the ear.

clue.text: House of wax

parts.note: bees build their home from wax combs

explanation.surface: A waxworks museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House of wax' suggests a waxworks; it is the home bees build from wax.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees build their home of waxen comb.

clue.text: The judge's decision is to hang first, then commute punishment

parts.note: to suspend is to hang something up
a sentence is the punishment handed down by a court

explanation.surface: A harsh judge rules for hanging first, then softens the penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests execution then leniency; in fact to suspend a sentence is to defer it, and 'commute' only colours the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A court ruling that defers a penalty is a decision made from the bench.
